entities.name: Álpin de Dalriada
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Álpin de Dalriada (áldalriða) was the king of the Picts from 726–728 CE, ruling jointly with Drest VII. The Pictish Chronicle lists place Alpín and Drest in a five-year joint rule.

This Pictish monarch played a crucial role in the history of Scotland during the Late Antiquity period. His reign overlapped with that of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of Northumbria and Mercia, and his kingdom's interactions with these powers had significant cultural and political implications.

The legacy of Álpin de Dalriada can be seen in the continued development of Pictish art and architecture during this period. His court may have influenced the work of Irish monks who came to Scotland during this time, leading to a unique blend of Pictish and Irish styles.

The significance of Álpin de Dalriada's rule lies in its impact on the formation of medieval Scotland. The kingdom's continued existence as a distinct entity despite the rise of Christian kingdoms like Northumbria reflects the resilience of pre-Christian cultures in Scotland.
